label: GO after a rewarded rare a1->S2 trial, late in episode (trial >= 80), when policy is not strongly committed to a2
explanation: Fires only at GO steps (never D1/D2), and essentially only when the previous trial was a1 with a rare transition to S2 that was rewarded (prev_action=1, prev_common=0, prev_reward=1 cover ~91% of mass; the rest are window-first trials where prev info is unknown). It is also restricted to the end of the episode: zero activations before trial 70, most from trial 80 on, with matching low value-head outputs (all activations have value < 7.13). Base condition alone gives precision 0.11; adding ep_trial >= 80 gives 0.53; adding the policy logit choice > -3 (agent not strongly choosing to switch to a2, the model-based response) gives F1 0.81 on dev. Never fires after a2 trials, after common transitions, or after unrewarded trials. Uses only observed history plus the agent own current policy logit, no future variables. Magnitude was not separately modeled; top activations are mostly where the agent stays with a1.

issues: All factual claims checked out on test: phase != GO precision 0; after a2 trials, 3 of 1473 test activations (precision 0.0); after common transitions, 3 of 1473 (precision 0.0); after unrewarded trials, 0; ep_trial < 70, 0; value >= 7.13, 0. Test scores reproduce: P 0.761, R 0.845, F1 0.801, mass recall 0.899.
Dev ablation chain also reproduces: previous-trial condition alone gives P 0.111 / F1 0.197; adding ep_trial >= 80 gives P 0.527 / F1 0.654; adding choice > -3 gives F1 0.807.

The remaining misses (about 8.7% of mass) are almost all at rel -3 GO, where prev_action is -1 (the previous trial is outside the window). They cannot be predicted: adding (prev_action == -1) & prev_reward == 1 to the predicate drops dev precision to 0.21 (F1 0.34). This is a data limit, not a gap in the label.

The late-episode condition is a graded ramp, not a step at trial 80. Precision within the predicate is 0.49 for trials 80-84 and 0.93 for trials >= 90 (with choice > -4). Trials 75-79 give precision 0.20-0.31. Most false positives are therefore early in the 80s. Thresholds on ep_trial + k*choice did not beat the original predicate (best dev F1 0.728 vs 0.807).

No systematic false-positive class by good state, start_high, since_rev, rel or the reward two trials back. Precision stays between 0.71 and 0.93 across these slices. Precision is higher when the trial two back was unrewarded (0.93) and lower when it was rewarded (0.73), but that is a modulation, not a separate class.

No future variables are used. choice is the agent's current policy logit at GO, which it computes itself. Note: ep_trial >= 80 assumes the GRU tracks a trial clock, which is plausible but is only a correlational description.
